## 4c1d80c25a99

**Suspected shortcut / distribution mismatch, not a wrong-label claim.**
Generator SHA-256
`2fe3bf8a15ae1ca7cb441755ab5b50d0acc16f12b1e23584ccd2a8d2dc2f2cfb`.
All three canonical inputs have a complete single-color wall perimeter.  Across
100 deterministic samples in each of easy, medium, and hard, **0/300** generated
inputs had a complete wall perimeter.  The retained generated witness is accepted
by the Racket authority, so the issue is transfer risk: training can learn the
internal full-row/full-column partition style without seeing the enclosed-room
geometry used by every canonical example.

Evidence: `checks/audit/4c1d80c25a99-perimeter-drift.json`,
`checks/audit/4c1d80c25a99-generated-racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/4c1d80c25a99-battery/checks/4c1d80c25a99_before_battery_summary.json`.
The battery independently flags distribution drift and reports three failed
stages (`lint`, `defect_lint`, `override`) plus advisory profile and semantic
stages.  I checked wall layout, canonical profiles, exact controls, self-check,
rule smoke, and authority synchronization; I left this audit-only target
unchanged.
